author: reek
body: The boot selector across reboots. The design's Failure Matrix is the spec, and every row of it that the selector owns is a line of output here.

author: reek
body: A reboot is simulated by calling boot-run again against the SAME flash, which is the honest model: the record survives because it is in flash, not because a variable was kept. Nothing is threaded between boots -- each call re-reads the record it finds. If persistence were fake, the attempt count could not climb.

author: reek
body: The image is real bytes in a real bank, the digest is a real SHA-256 of what landed there, and the flag word is a real single-word flash program.

author: reek
body: Put an image in a slot through the Flash effect, exactly as the LwM2M client would.

author: reek
body: A wiped record: the factory state, and also what a power loss during the first write leaves behind.

author: reek
body: Row: after commit (7). B is marked, boots, commits, and is primary from then on.

author: reek
body: Row: during first boot of new image (6-7). B is marked and never commits -- the image boots and wedges. Each reboot spends an attempt; past the limit the device abandons it and returns to A.

author: reek
body: Row: after flag, before/during reboot (5) -- on fail boots old. The candidate is marked with a correct digest and THEN the bank is corrupted (a bad cell, a partial write). The selector hashes what is actually in the bank, so it catches it and never runs it.

author: reek
body: Row: during Gate B (4) -- candidate flag never set. Also the power-loss case: a wiped record has no marker, so there is no candidate to run.
